svg.title: Cross-Sector Watchlist Master Scorecard · Four-Quadrant
svg.desc: X axis = advantage strength = (quality_moat + growth_driver) / 2; Y axis = cost control = (valuation_setup + risk_control) / 2. The all-market chart is for cross-theme navigation only; valuation is still compared within each sector basket.
svg.text: X = Advantage strength = (quality + growth) / 2 · Y = Cost control = (valuation + risk) / 2
Note: the all-market chart is for cross-theme navigation only. Use sector charts below for company-level judgments.

g.title: MSFT — Microsoft Platform Technology and Internet Buy | Total score 21 Advantage strength 5 / Cost control 3.5 Enterprise distribution control and Azure AI monetization path are the clearest; although premium, it remains the high-conviction core position in the platform basket.

NVDA — NVIDIA Semiconductors and Foundational Compute Buy | Total score 20 Advantage strength 5 / Cost control 3 Platform position is the strongest, and even if it is not cheap it remains the hardest-to-replace core thesis in this group.

APO — Apollo Global Management Financial Institutions and Capital Markets Buy | Total score 20 Advantage strength 4 / Cost control 3.5 The permanent capital + private credit engine is the most complete, and current valuation has not yet become distorted.

AMZN — Amazon Platform Technology and Internet Buy | Total score 19 Advantage strength 4.5 / Cost control 4 The AWS + ads + retail triple-engine is still working, and on the platform basket basis this valuation is not the tightest.

GOOG — Alphabet Platform Technology and Internet Buy | Total score 19 Advantage strength 4.5 / Cost control 3.5 Search cash flow gives enough cushion, and Cloud AI continues to improve growth structure, making value alignment relatively balanced.

META — Meta Platforms Platform Technology and Internet Buy | Total score 19 Advantage strength 4.5 / Cost control 3.5 The ad engine and AI efficiency gains are both working, but high CapEx and regulatory pressure keep it slightly below the most stable platform position.

TSM — Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Semiconductors and Foundational Compute Buy | Total score 19 Advantage strength 4.5 / Cost control 3.5 Advanced manufacturing and advanced packaging infrastructure are scarce, and current valuation can still be partially offset by geographic discounting.

AVGO — Broadcom Semiconductors and Foundational Compute Buy | Total score 19 Advantage strength 4.5 / Cost control 3 Custom XPU + networking dual positioning makes earnings realization more direct; concentration is high but it still belongs in the first tier.

V — Visa Financial Institutions and Capital Markets Buy | Total score 19 Advantage strength 4.5 / Cost control 3.5 The best quality and hardest business model, despite not being cheap, is still the long-term top pick in this financial basket.

SOFI — SoFi Technologies Fintech and Consumer Credit Buy | Total score 19 Advantage strength 4 / Cost control 3.5 In this high-risk fintech basket, balance among platform breadth, bank license, and monetization path is the best.

REGN — Regeneron Pharma and Biotechnology Buy | Total score 19 Advantage strength 4 / Cost control 3.5 Platform biotech quality is high, valuation is not extreme, and risk-adjusted reward is better than high-expectation large pharma.

AAPL — Apple Platform Technology and Internet Hold | Total score 18 Advantage strength 4 / Cost control 3 Quality is exceptional, but it currently behaves more like a mature platform defensive position; AI-driven re-acceleration remains to be confirmed.

MU — Micron Technology Semiconductors and Foundational Compute Hold | Total score 18 Advantage strength 4 / Cost control 4 HBM tailwind is most clear, but strong cyclical nature of memory means this is a high-quality cyclical holding rather than a long-horizon best solution.

JPM — JPMorgan Chase Financial Institutions and Capital Markets Hold | Total score 18 Advantage strength 4 / Cost control 4 Most stable large-bank sample, but regulatory discount means it is more of a quality anchor than strongest elastic buy point.

BAC — Bank of America Financial Institutions and Capital Markets Hold | Total score 18 Advantage strength 3.5 / Cost control 4 Valuation is cheap, but quality and earnings elasticity still trail JPM slightly.

QCOM — Qualcomm Semiconductors and Foundational Compute Hold / no-chase | Total score 17 Advantage strength 4 / Cost control 3 Physical AI + data-center inference evidence has improved, but financial proof is still missing and the current price is already in the no-chase zone.

GSK — GSK Pharma and Biotechnology Hold | Total score 17 Advantage strength 3.5 / Cost control 4 Value re-rating and pipeline progress are underway, but execution is still needed before upgrading to Buy.

AMD — Advanced Micro Devices Semiconductors and Foundational Compute Hold | Total score 16 Advantage strength 4 / Cost control 2.5 The second-position story is valid, but software ecosystem and scaling realization still need further proof.

BX — Blackstone Financial Institutions and Capital Markets Hold | Total score 16 Advantage strength 4 / Cost control 2 Platform breadth is strong, but when exit and fundraising cycles turn, volatility can be more direct.

PGY — Pagaya Technologies Fintech and Consumer Credit Hold | Total score 16 Advantage strength 3 / Cost control 3.5 Valuation and funding tailwind gives a good setup, but partner and funding concentration are still too high.

LLY — Eli Lilly Pharma and Biotechnology Hold | Total score 16 Advantage strength 5 / Cost control 1.5 Growth is strongest, but high expectations plus policy/supply sensitivity make current odds less comfortable than they seem.

TXN — Texas Instruments Semiconductors and Foundational Compute Hold | Total score 15 Advantage strength 3 / Cost control 3.5 Quality is solid but AI resilience is limited, making it more a base holding than this group’s lead entry.

GS — Goldman Sachs Financial Institutions and Capital Markets Hold | Total score 15 Advantage strength 3.5 / Cost control 3 Cyclical elasticity is clear, but dependence on market activity revival is higher.

HOOD — Robinhood Markets Fintech and Consumer Credit Hold | Total score 15 Advantage strength 4 / Cost control 1.5 User entry is strong, but current price already factors in too much trading sentiment and adjacency optionality.
MRK — Merck Pharma and Biotechnology Hold | Total score 15 Advantage strength 3.5 / Cost control 2.5 Cash flow is still strong, but succession pace after patent cliffs keeps it at a middle ranking.

MRVL — Marvell Technology Semiconductors and Foundational Compute Hold | Total score 14 Advantage strength 3.5 / Cost control 2 Good elasticity but high concentration; odds are decent but value still lags leaders and infrastructure layer.

AFRM — Affirm Holdings Fintech and Consumer Credit Hold | Total score 14 Advantage strength 3 / Cost control 2.5 BNPL positioning remains, but funding costs and credit performance keep it from the first tier.

ARM — Arm Holdings Semiconductors and Foundational Compute Sell | Total score 13 Advantage strength 4 / Cost control 1.5 Scarcity is strong, but valuation has already priced in too much good news in advance, leaving little safety margin.

UPST — Upstart Holdings Fintech and Consumer Credit Sell | Total score 13 Advantage strength 2.5 / Cost control 2.5 Short-term sentiment is hottest, but funding supply and credit risk still outweigh the technology story.

TSLA — Tesla Platform Technology and Internet Sell | Total score 12 Advantage strength 3 / Cost control 1 Long optionality is large, but mismatch between auto cash flow and extreme valuation remains the hardest risk here.

HSBC — HSBC Holdings Financial Institutions and Capital Markets Sell | Total score 12 Advantage strength 2.5 / Cost control 2.5 Too many geography and restructuring variables, and even at modest valuation there is no best risk/reward.

CVS — CVS Health Pharma and Biotechnology Sell | Total score 12 Advantage strength 2.5 / Cost control 3 It appears cheap, but policy, loss ratio, and PBM risk make it the weakest risk-adjusted setup in this group.

INTC — Intel Semiconductors and Foundational Compute Sell | Total score 11 Advantage strength 2.5 / Cost control 1 Transformation odds are large, but triple execution risk across product, manufacturing, and capex is highest.
KLAR — Klarna Group Fintech and Consumer Credit Sell | Total score 11 Advantage strength 3 / Cost control 1.5 Brand awareness is good, but earnings visibility and valuation matching remain weak.

SNDK — Sandisk Semiconductors and Foundational Compute Sell | Total score 9 Advantage strength 2 / Cost control 2 More like a NAND cycle ticket than an AI core thesis, and standalone sample period remains too short.
